note: No finding has status verified_test: supporting tests were identified but not executed in this project.

findings.question: Is the client/server boundary structurally enforced?
findings.method: REA analyze-javascript-application on playwright-core/src; derived import matrix from graph edges (research/rea-evidence/derive_dirmatrix.mjs)
findings.evidence: No 'client -> server' key in matrix; client -> @protocol 15, remote -> server 21, server -> generated 26
findings.interpretation: Client never imports server code; they communicate via generated protocol types
remaining_questions: REA graph coverage is partial; dynamic requires not seen

findings.question: How does a public API call become an RPC with timeout/abort?
findings.evidence: _createChannel proxy -> _wrapApiCall(apiZone) -> connection.sendMessageToServer; metadata{title,location,internal,timeout}; AbortSignal -> '__abort__' message (connection.ts:206-215)
findings.interpretation: Single-RPC-per-API-call with zone-based attribution

findings.question: What does the server do per dispatched call?
findings.rea_tool: trace-javascript-semantics (forward-influence on DispatcherConnection.dispatch: only 'awaits' relations recovered; 47 unknowns)
findings.evidence: validate params/metadata; ProgressController per call id; onBeforeCall(3s); controller.run(method, timeout); serializeError + compressCallLog; onAfterCall(3s); slowMo
findings.interpretation: Instrumentation brackets every call; abort looked up by call id
remaining_questions: exact line numbers are approximate (range read, not pinned)

findings.question: What is Progress?
findings.evidence: deadline timer rejects _forceAbortPromise and aborts AbortController; race() adds force-abort to every await; log accumulates metadata.log
findings.interpretation: Cancellation is cooperative at await points via race()

findings.question: What is the shared retry/backoff policy?
findings.evidence: backoff [20,50,100,100,500] with 0 prepended; popped when > timeout/5; non-retriable: abort, JS error, closed session, non-recoverable DOM error, invalid selector, detached
findings.interpretation: Single polling primitive used by actions, expect, waitForSelector

findings.question: How does Chromium communication work?
findings.evidence: CRConnection multiplexes CRSession by sessionId; child sessions via Target.attachedToTarget
findings.interpretation: CDP session tree under one transport

findings.question: What happens on goto?
findings.evidence: navigation events collected before navigateFrame; documentId matching; NavigationAbortedError on interruption; lifecycle wait
findings.interpretation: Race-safe navigation by document id

findings.question: What is the actionability sequence for a click?
findings.evidence: visible/enabled/stable/non-inert in page; scroll cycling; hit-target interceptor; waitForSignalsCreatedBy
findings.interpretation: Pre-action checks + post-action navigation wait

findings.question: Is instrumentation a bus shared by tracing/inspector/runner?
findings.evidence: Tracing implements InstrumentationListener; onBeforeCall appends event synchronously then snapshots
findings.interpretation: Trace is produced by an instrumentation listener

findings.question: What does expect do server-side?
findings.evidence: one-shot null-progress check then backoff; on not-found captures body ARIA snapshot; ExpectError details
findings.interpretation: Web-first assertion polling is server-side and returns diagnostic context

findings.question: Overlay/interstitial handling hook?
findings.evidence: user-registered selector+callback run at pre-check; action waits for hidden unless noWaitAfter
findings.interpretation: Only built-in adaptive hook; user code, not diagnosis-driven

findings.question: Does playwright-core already ship an agent tool backend?
findings.evidence: 49 backend files incl. snapshot.ts, verify.ts, response.ts, tab.ts, codegen.ts, find.ts, wait.ts; cli-client, cli-daemon, mcp, skills, trace
findings.interpretation: MCP/CLI agent surface lives in core and builds on the public API

findings.question: Snapshot format for agents?
findings.evidence: inputs target/filename/depth/boxes; runtime output '- button "Save" [active] [ref=e2]'
findings.interpretation: Compact ARIA tree with stable per-snapshot refs; depth and bounding boxes optional

findings.question: What verification tools exist in the agent backend?
findings.evidence: capability 'testing'; verify_element_visible/text_visible/list_visible use getByRole/getByText count>0; return 'Done' or error
findings.interpretation: Agent-invoked existence/visibility checks via same page handle; no independent verifier
remaining_questions: rest of file (value/other tools) not fully read

findings.question: Does the snapshot response support incremental updates?
findings.evidence: _includeSnapshot: 'none'|'full'|'explicit'; config snapshot.mode
findings.interpretation: No delta mode in this file (Phase 2 fork found agent-browser has one)
remaining_questions: other files may implement diffs (not exhaustively searched)

findings.question: Does the agent backend convert actions into test code?
findings.evidence: actions recorded as ActionInContext; rendered to typescript/python/java/csharp as 'Ran Playwright code' with secret substitution
findings.interpretation: Exploration->code primitive exists; promotion/review/assertion independence is not part of it

findings.question: How are test timeouts attributed?
findings.evidence: messages differ for test, hook, fixture setup/teardown, worker teardown, modifier
findings.interpretation: Timeout slots per runnable type

findings.question: How is error-context.md generated?
findings.evidence: only on errors; page.ariaSnapshot({mode:'ai',timeout:5000}) from first page of context unless matcher already provided errorContext; markdown with fixed fix-it prompt
findings.interpretation: Runner ships an LLM-oriented failure brief; snapshot taken at context close (source TODO admits it may be wrong page/time)

findings.question: Artifacts on failure
findings.evidence: per failing test: trace.zip, test-failed-1.png, error-context.md; trace.zip entries 0-trace.trace, 1-trace.trace, test.trace, *.network, *.stacks, screencast/, src/, attachments/

findings.question: How does the scheduler reuse workers?
findings.evidence: prefers free worker with same workerHash
findings.interpretation: Fixture-compatible worker reuse

findings.question: Sharding granularity
findings.evidence: shards by test groups; parallel files per test, serial files whole
findings.interpretation: Group-level sharding with optional weights

findings.question: Can REA recover class-method call edges?
findings.evidence: 0 relations; unknown reason 'dynamic-call: Unsupported MemberExpression call target' at frames.ts:1150
findings.interpretation: REA's static call graph does not resolve this.method() calls in these classes; contradicts expectation that REA gives full call graphs here
remaining_questions: Would a different seed kind or include_ambiguous_dynamic_edges help? not tried

findings.question: Is REA semantic coverage complete for playwright-core/src?
findings.evidence: semantic_graph coverage partial/truncated at node ceiling 100000; function nodes cover 101 modules; frames.ts and dom.ts absent
findings.interpretation: Needed a separate slice analysis (copies of 24 files) for core execution files

findings.question: Where does playwright-mcp's implementation live?
findings.evidence: src/README.md says source is in the Playwright monorepo; index.js re-exports tools.createConnection from playwright-core/lib/coreBundle.
findings.interpretation: playwright-mcp is a packaging/test repo; behaviour is in playwright-core/src/tools.

findings.question: What tool/capability model do Playwright agent tools use?
findings.evidence: zod-typed tools with capability (core/testing/core-input) and type (readOnly/input/assertion); click calls response.setIncludeSnapshot() then tab.waitForCompletion(locator.click).
findings.interpretation: Typed, capability-gated tool surface; every input tool can attach a snapshot to its response.
remaining_questions: runtime token size of responses not measured

findings.question: Does Playwright's agent interface support incremental snapshots?
findings.method: direct read of config type and response builder
findings.evidence: snapshot.mode is 'full' | 'none'; response _includeSnapshot is 'none'|'full'|'explicit'.
findings.interpretation: No delta/incremental mode in the pinned commit. Impact on tokens is a hypothesis.
findings.confidence: high for absence in these files
remaining_questions: whether other code paths diff snapshots (e.g. tabs header changes only)

findings.question: How does Playwright's agent layer decide an action has settled?
findings.evidence: settleMs default 500; if a navigation request occurred waits load<=10s; else awaits responses of tracked requests raced against a 5s timer, then settle again.
findings.interpretation: Heuristic settle, not a semantic postcondition.

findings.question: What verification exists in Playwright's agent tools?
findings.evidence: Four assertion-type tools (element visible by role+name, text visible, list visible, value) gated by capability 'testing'; failures returned as response errors; success emits assertion actions for codegen.
findings.interpretation: Verification is explicit and caller-driven, not bound to the preceding action.

findings.question: What does Playwright's healer agent do on failure?
findings.evidence: Prompt: run tests, debug, edit selectors/assertions, rerun; mark test.fixme() if confident the test is correct.
findings.interpretation: Recovery is prompt-driven test editing; no structural record of original failure beyond the agent's notes ('Document your findings').

findings.question: Can Playwright agent tools produce test code from exploration?
findings.evidence: Tools call response.addAction/addCode; --codegen selects typescript/python/java/csharp.
findings.interpretation: Exploration-to-code path exists; quality of generated tests untested.

findings.question: Is Playwright MCP origin filtering a security boundary?
findings.evidence: Options text: 'does not serve as a security boundary and does not affect redirects'; secrets 'a convenience and not a security feature'; README: 'Playwright MCP is not a security boundary'.
findings.interpretation: Documented by the project itself; defensive isolation must come from the host.

findings.question: What failure artifacts do Playwright agent tools persist?
findings.evidence: SessionLog writes session.md under an output folder; tracing.ts exists (not read in detail).
findings.interpretation: Session log and trace tooling exist; schema/contents of replay not examined.

findings.question: Does browser-use depend on Playwright?
findings.evidence: depends on cdp-use==1.4.5; pytest-playwright-asyncio is commented out.
findings.interpretation: Uses its own CDP stack.

findings.question: What per-step contract and limits does the browser-use agent have?
findings.evidence: max_failures=5, max_actions_per_step=5, enable_planning, loop detection; output requires evaluation_previous_goal, memory, next_goal, action.
findings.interpretation: Self-evaluation is part of the LLM output, i.e. agent-claimed.

findings.question: Does the browser-use judge override the agent's self-reported success?
findings.evidence: Docstring: judge verdict is attached but does NOT override last_result.success; telemetry sends both.
findings.interpretation: Independent judgement exists but is report-only and LLM-based.

findings.question: How does browser-use replay saved history?
findings.evidence: Replays steps with max_retries, skip_failures, element validation; extract steps re-evaluated by an LLM 'AI step'; save_history writes file.
findings.interpretation: Replay is of agent history, not a reviewable test file.

findings.question: How does browser-use restrict domains?
findings.evidence: URL checked against allowed_domains/prohibited_domains; tests in tests/ci/security.
findings.interpretation: Navigation-level filtering; subresource behaviour not examined.

findings.question: What replay/diagnostic artifacts does browser-use produce?
findings.evidence: gif.py and history items exist.
findings.interpretation: History and GIF only; schema contents not read.

findings.question: Does agent-browser need Playwright/Node at runtime?
findings.evidence: Pure Rust daemon with direct CDP; engines chrome, lightpanda, obscura; Safari via WebDriver.
findings.interpretation: Independent of Playwright; mostly Chromium-protocol based.

findings.question: What observation-compaction options does agent-browser offer?
findings.evidence: -i, -c, -d, -s, --urls, --delta (full / unchanged / structural delta; falls back to full after URL change or no savings).
findings.interpretation: Delta snapshots exist in a competitor; token savings unmeasured here.

findings.question: Does agent-browser model uncertain outcomes?
findings.evidence: Mutating commands are not re-sent after daemon receipt; failure code outcome_unknown.
findings.interpretation: Explicit unknown-outcome state.
remaining_questions: is it surfaced consistently across commands

findings.question: What security controls does agent-browser implement?
findings.evidence: Domain allowlist covering subresources/WebSocket/beacon with WebRTC disabled; content boundaries; max-output; JSON action policy (allow/deny/confirm); confirm-actions env.
findings.interpretation: Most comprehensive documented controls among studied tools; enforcement not tested.

findings.question: What evals/benchmarks ship with agent-browser?
findings.evidence: benchmarks: daemon command latency Node vs Rust in Vercel Sandbox; evals: skill loading/selection/command usage and CLI-vs-MCP context footprint, optional LLM judge.
findings.interpretation: Measure tool ergonomics and latency, not defect detection.

findings.question: What is Stagehand v4's architecture?
findings.evidence: SDKs send JSON-RPC (act/observe/extract) to a Chrome extension service-worker runtime; services/actService.ts etc. contain LLM logic; own CDP 'understudy' layer.
findings.interpretation: Not Playwright-based in v4; LLM logic runs in the extension runtime.

findings.question: Does Stagehand cache or replay actions?
findings.evidence: HTTP cache routes keyed by url and AX tree with LLM-usage savings metadata; act accepts a prior Action for deterministic execution; replayCachedActions function exists.
findings.interpretation: Replay/caching reduces LLM calls; cache requires a Stagehand API endpoint.

findings.question: What does Stagehand selfHeal do and record?
findings.evidence: selfHeal defaults false; on non-timeout error re-captures snapshot, asks LLM for an element, retries; failure messages replace the original; success returns new selector.
findings.interpretation: Recovery can change the target without carrying the original error in the result.
remaining_questions: whether logger output preserves the original error (logger.debug exists at line ~380)

findings.question: Does Stagehand act verify outcomes?
findings.evidence: success is returned after performUnderstudyMethod does not throw; no post-action check seen in these functions.
findings.interpretation: Likely no independent verification in act; two-step path diffs trees (line 203) but for planning, not verification.

findings.question: Which exploration-to-test features does Stagehand have?
findings.evidence: observe returns Actions; act(Action) executes without LLM.
findings.interpretation: Replayable action objects, not generated test files.

findings.question: How does Stagehand restrict domains?
findings.evidence: Allowed/blocked domain rules normalized into CDP Fetch request patterns.
findings.interpretation: Request-level interception via CDP.

findings.question: What evaluation assets does Stagehand ship?
findings.evidence: datasets: hardbenchmark, odysseysbench, onlineMind2Web, webtailbench, webvoyager; scoring.ts, pricing/.
findings.interpretation: Task-success benchmarks with pricing support; not read in depth.

findings.question: How does Midscene assert outcomes?
findings.evidence: Model returns boolean+thought; false throws 'Assertion failed … Reason …' unless keepRawResponse.
findings.interpretation: LLM-judged assertion with a stated reason; deterministic checks are the caller's job.

findings.question: Is Skyvern relevant and reusable?
findings.evidence: AGPL-3.0; Python; vision-LLM workflow automation with a Playwright-compatible SDK.
findings.interpretation: Relevant as a competitor; AGPL limits code reuse. Implementation not studied.

findings.question: Is magnitudedev/magnitude a browser testing agent?
findings.evidence: Current description: open source local LLM inference engine.
findings.interpretation: Not a competitor for this project; earlier assumption contradicted by current repo state.

findings.question: Does Playwright ship an agent-friendly trace reader?
findings.method: experiment: npx playwright trace open/actions/errors on sample trace (1.64.1)
findings.evidence: Subcommands open|close|actions|action|requests|request|console|errors|snapshot|screenshot|attachments|install-skill. actions output 1,688 bytes (16 rows with durations, failed row marked); errors output 742 bytes with full call log
findings.interpretation: Compact terminal trace inspection already exists; failure diagnosis for a 2-action test costs ~2.4 KB of text

findings.question: Trace NDJSON event types in a real trace
findings.evidence: 1-trace.trace types: context-options 1, before 3, event 1, after 3, screencast-frame 3, frame-snapshot 4, log 29 (44 events, 7,642 bytes). test.trace: before 18, after 18, error 1 (38 events)
findings.interpretation: Trace contains per-call before/after, DOM frame-snapshots, screencast frames and log lines; runner-side steps in separate test.trace
remaining_questions: aria-snapshot events appear only in some configurations (not in this sample)

findings.question: Are aria refs stable across a DOM insertion?
findings.evidence: After inserting a new first button, existing elements kept refs (A=e2,B=e3); new got e5; locator(aria-ref=e3) still clicked B
findings.interpretation: Refs are bound to element identity, not position, within a page session for this one mutation type
remaining_questions: re-render replacing nodes, navigation, iframes untested

findings.question: Does the trace CLI offer re-execution of the failing flow?
findings.evidence: No replay/rerun subcommand; snapshot subcommand runs a playwright-cli command against a DOM snapshot
findings.interpretation: Trace is inspectable but not re-drivable by this CLI
remaining_questions: other entry points (UI mode time travel) not checked

findings.question: Does a Playwright context.route handler see HTTP redirect hops?
findings.source_path: benchmarks/test/integration.test.ts (policy under a real browser); packages/adapter-playwright/src/index.ts applyPolicy
findings.evidence: With a plain route handler allowing only 127.0.0.1, goto /redirect?to=http://localhost:PORT/__oracle ended on the disallowed host with a 200 response (network log: 302 then 200 for localhost). Validating each hop via route.fetch({maxRedirects:0}) blocked it; fulfilling a 3xx directly broke allowed redirects (chrome-error), so GET/HEAD chains are pre-validated then route.continue()
findings.interpretation: Origin filtering by route alone is not a security boundary for redirects (consistent with Playwright MCP docs statement P2-008)
remaining_questions: POST redirect chains, WebSockets, service workers not covered

findings.question: What do @playwright/mcp action responses contain by default?
findings.evidence: Response lists Ran Playwright code, Page URL/Title, console counts and a link to a snapshot file (.playwright-mcp/page-*.yml) instead of inline snapshot; browser_snapshot returns it; 25 tools incl. browser_find, browser_fill_form, browser_run_code_unsafe
findings.interpretation: Agents must request or read the snapshot explicitly; observation cost depends on actor policy
remaining_questions: config options that inline snapshots not tried

findings.question: Observation size, scripted actors, same form task
findings.evidence: See results.md: on a 400-row page median chars read: MCP re-snapshot 113549, MCP snapshot-once 38379, AF outline 24137, AF controls 876, AF controls+delta 422
findings.interpretation: Bounded task-relevant observations are far smaller than full snapshots for this task and page; effect on model accuracy not measured; chars/4 is only a rough token proxy
remaining_questions: real-world pages, real actors, tokenizer-measured tokens

findings.question: Do framework semantics reduce false passes and duplicates vs Playwright configurations on the seeded scenarios?
findings.method: benchmarks/harness n=20 x 15 scenarios x 5 drivers, two runs (frozen, post-fix)
findings.evidence: Post-fix (1500 trials, 0 harness errors): defect scenarios missed: pw-trust 40%, pw-test 40%, pw-strong 0%, pw-heal-naive 60%, vedha 0%; effect scenarios reported fail with no effect: 20%, 30%, 30%, 20%, 0%. Frozen run: vedha scored 0/20 on S12 (uncertain, input step without postcondition) and its label check matched a longer label; fixed afterwards.
findings.interpretation: On these author-built scenarios the semantics behave as designed; hold-out (S12-S15) result was mixed before fixes; generalisation untested
remaining_questions: hold-out scenarios; LLM actors; real apps

findings.question: Do Vedha and the Playwright adapter behave the same on Firefox and WebKit?
findings.method: integration tests (15) and benchmark track xb-firefox/xb-webkit (n=5, 15 scenarios, vedha vs pw-strong) with VEDHA_BROWSER
findings.evidence: All 15 integration tests pass on both engines (incl. policy: redirects, POST redirect, WebSocket, service workers). Benchmark: vedha 75/75 correct on each; pw-strong 60/75 on each, failing S04, S05, S10 as on Chromium. Playwright error message classification worked unchanged on both engines.
findings.interpretation: No engine-specific differences observed on this fixture
remaining_questions: small n; fixture only; real sites untested

findings.question: Do upstream Playwright tests covering the scenarios we traced pass on the pinned source?
findings.method: built pinned commit in an isolated copy; ran 9 page spec files (click, locator-click, goto, expect-timeout, add-locator-handler, wait-for-selector-1, aria-snapshot-ai, click-timeout-1/2) and 6 runner spec files (timeout, retry, shard, fixtures, expect, trace)
findings.evidence: Page specs: 264 expected, 1 skipped, 0 unexpected, 0 flaky. Runner specs: 196 expected, 0 unexpected, 0 flaky
findings.interpretation: The supporting tests for traced scenarios T2-T6 pass on the pinned source; they exercised the same code paths we cite
remaining_questions: Firefox/WebKit upstream projects not run; other spec files not run

findings.question: Does runtime behaviour on 1.65.0-next (pinned source build) match what we observed on published 1.64.1?
findings.method: re-ran research/experiments/pw-runtime/exp1.mjs against the built source
findings.evidence: missingTimeout, waitedForDone, aria identical; clickTimeout identical except the last retry block repeated 3x instead of 2x (poll count within the time window)
findings.interpretation: Findings from 1.64.1 hold on the pinned source; the only difference is timing-dependent repetition count
